subject: CS301
text: What is the time complexity of reading the element at a given index of an array?
explanation: An array stores its elements side by side, so the place of any index is worked out directly.

subject: CS301
text: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search in an array of n elements?
explanation: In the worst case the element is last or missing, so all n elements are checked.

subject: CS301
text: Binary search can be used on an array only when the array is…
explanation: Binary search halves the range by comparing with the middle element, which only works on sorted data.

subject: CS301
text: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on n sorted elements?
explanation: Each comparison halves the remaining range, so about log₂ n comparisons are needed.

subject: CS301
text: How long does it take to insert an element at the start of an array that holds n elements?
explanation: Every existing element must move one place to the right to make room.

subject: CS301
text: Which notation gives an upper bound on how fast an algorithm's running time grows?
explanation: Big O gives an upper bound. Big Omega gives a lower bound, and Big Theta a bound from both sides.

subject: CS301
text: Which data structure works on the first in, first out principle?
explanation: A queue removes items in the order they were added: the first one in is the first one out.

subject: CS301
text: Which operation removes the top element of a stack?
explanation: Pop removes and returns the top element. Peek only looks at it, and push adds one.

subject: CS301
text: Which data structure does breadth-first search use to remember the vertices to visit next?
explanation: Breadth-first search visits vertices level by level, so it needs a queue: vertices found first are explored first.

subject: CS301
text: How long does it take to insert a node at the head of a singly linked list?
explanation: Only the new node's pointer and the head pointer change, whatever the length of the list.

subject: CS301
text: Which data structure is used to evaluate a postfix expression?
explanation: Operands are pushed on a stack. Each operator pops its operands and pushes the result back.

subject: CS301
text: In a circular queue stored in an array of size n, with one slot kept empty, when is the queue full?
explanation: One slot is kept empty, so the queue is full when the slot after rear is front.

subject: CS301
text: Which structure allows insertion and deletion at both ends?
explanation: A deque, or double-ended queue, allows adding and removing at the front and at the back.

subject: CS301
text: Reversing a singly linked list in place takes how much time and extra space?
explanation: One pass re-points every node at the node before it, using three pointers and no extra list.

subject: CS301
text: Which of these is not a typical use of a stack?
explanation: Breadth-first search needs a queue. The other three all rely on last in, first out.

subject: CS301
text: How long does it take to reach the k-th node of a singly linked list?
explanation: A linked list has no index. You must follow k pointers from the head.

subject: CS301
text: What is the largest number of children a node of a binary tree can have?
explanation: By definition each node of a binary tree has at most two children: a left one and a right one.

subject: CS301
text: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in ascending order?
explanation: Inorder visits the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree. In a binary search tree that is ascending order.

subject: CS301
text: In a binary search tree, where are the keys that are smaller than a node's key?
explanation: Smaller keys go to the left and larger keys to the right. That rule is what makes searching fast.

subject: CS301
text: What is the worst-case time to search a binary search tree of n nodes that is not balanced?
explanation: A tree built from keys that arrive in sorted order becomes a chain, and searching a chain can check all n nodes.

subject: CS301
text: How many edges does a tree with n nodes have?
explanation: Every node except the root has exactly one edge to its parent, which gives n − 1 edges.

subject: CS301
text: Which traversal visits a node before both of its subtrees?
explanation: Preorder means node first, then the left subtree, then the right subtree.

subject: MA301
text: The statement “p AND q” is true when…
options: at least one of them is true
exactly one of them is true
both p and q are true
explanation: A conjunction is true only when every part of it is true.

subject: MA301
text: The implication “if p then q” is false only when…
options: p is false and q is true
p is true and q is false
explanation: A promise is broken only when its condition holds and its result does not.

subject: MA301
text: How many subsets does a set with 3 elements have?
explanation: A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets, and 2³ is 8. The empty set and the set itself are both counted.

subject: MA301
text: For A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {3, 4}, what is the intersection of A and B?
explanation: The intersection holds the elements that are in both sets. Only 3 is in both.

subject: MA301
text: Which law says that NOT (p AND q) is the same as (NOT p) OR (NOT q)?
explanation: De Morgan's laws turn the negation of an AND into an OR of negations, and the other way round.

subject: MA301
text: A statement that is true whatever the truth values of its parts is called a…
explanation: A tautology is always true, a contradiction is always false, and a contingency can be either.

subject: EC301
text: In Boolean algebra, what is A OR (NOT A)?
explanation: One of A and NOT A is always 1, and OR needs only one input to be 1.

subject: EC301
text: In Boolean algebra, what is A AND 0?
explanation: AND gives 1 only when every input is 1, and here one input is always 0.

subject: EC301
text: Which gate gives 1 only when both of its inputs are 1?
explanation: That is the definition of the AND gate.

subject: EC301
text: Which gate is called a universal gate, because any circuit can be built from it alone?
explanation: NOT, AND and OR can each be built from NAND gates, so NAND alone is enough. NOR is universal as well.

subject: EC301
text: What is the output of an XOR gate when both of its inputs are 1?
options: The same as the first input
explanation: XOR gives 1 when its inputs differ. Two equal inputs give 0.

subject: CS302
text: In object oriented programming, an object is…
explanation: A class describes what its objects hold and can do. An object is one thing made from that description.

subject: CS302
text: Which special method runs when an object is created?
explanation: The constructor sets up a new object, usually by giving its fields their first values.

subject: CS302
text: Keeping an object's data private and reaching it only through its methods is called…
explanation: Encapsulation keeps the data and the code that works on it together, and hides the data from outside.

subject: CS302
text: In Java, which keyword makes a member visible only inside its own class?
explanation: A private member can be used only by code in the same class.

subject: CS302
text: In Java, what does the keyword “this” refer to?
options: The method that called this one
explanation: Inside an instance method or a constructor, “this” is the object the method was called on.
